title: Progressive decimation + accessible summaries for interactive time-series
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Problem: High-density time-series (tens of thousands of points per trace) causes jank and degraded hover/tooltip fidelity in the console dashboards. Current strategies (full canvas render + simple pixel binning) either lose interactive hover accuracy or are too expensive on low-power devices. We need a design pattern and component updates that: 1) progressively decimates large traces for initial render to meet latency SLOs, 2) preserves high-fidelity interactive layers (hover, crosshair, legend highlights) when the user interacts, and 3) surfaces concise, screen-reader friendly summaries so keyboard/screen-reader users get equivalent insight without requiring high-cost rendering. Objectives: reduce initial render CPU on main dashboards by 2x+ for heavy traces, preserve sub-100ms hover latency on common laptop class CPUs, and meet WCAG ATK guidance for chart summaries and focus management.
acceptance_criteria: Initial viewport render of 1M-point aggregated trace reduces main-thread CPU by >=50% compared to baseline on macbook-pro-2019 (simulated).
Hover/crosshair reveal shows exact sampled point within 1px of visual trace after interaction (on devices tested).
Keyboard focus and screen-reader summary provide: min/max/time-of-max, moving-average over pinned window, and link to raw timebucket table (ARIA live region announcement).
Design tokens updated for decimation state (reduced-opacity, reduced-stroke) and interactive state (highlight stroke/token color) with token names documented.
Design review complete and component spec landed with usage examples and image-based regression tests in the storybook.
Performance smoke test added to CI that runs a headless render of a 250k-point series and asserts latency thresholds.
UX copy for accessible summaries approved by content designer.
design_decisions: Use progressive decimation on first paint: server-supplied aggregates when available, else client LTTB (largest triangle three buckets) fallback implemented in worker thread.
Keep two layers: visual overview layer (decimated, low-res) and interaction layer (sparse sampled indices) that hydrates on first pointer or keyboard focus.
Tooltips use the interaction layer for exact values; when hydrated, interactive layer will request a small-range re-render at full fidelity for the hovered window only.

Accessibility: expose a concise summary via an ARIA live region when a chart gains keyboard focus; summary includes data density, visible span, min/max and time of peak. Provide a keyboard-only drilldown modal for table view.
Animations limited during decimation transitions to avoid layout thrashing; use alpha fades instead of reflowing SVG paths.
Design tokens: add tokens.chart.decimation.opacity, tokens.chart.interaction.strokeWidth, tokens.chart.decimation.strokeStyle for consistent theming across variants.
open_questions: Should decimation be a default opt-in on all console timeseries or gated behind a 'perf mode' toggle?
Server vs client: prefer server-provided summaries for enterprise customers with very large traces. How do we detect and prefer server aggregates?
Edge cases for multiple overlays (annotations + multi-series) — does interaction-layer hydration scale linearly? Need engineering input on memory cost.
